title: Underlying equivalences and operadic colimits of coherent modules
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functors, mapping spaces and universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and monoidal infinity-categories of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category]. Let $\mathcal V$ be a monoidal infinity-category and $\mathcal M$ an infinity-category with a coherent left action $\otimes:\mathcal V\times\mathcal M\to\mathcal M$: the equivalences $(v\otimes w)\otimes m\simeq v\otimes(w\otimes m)$ and $\mathbf1\otimes m\simeq m$ include all associative and unital higher compatibilities. An associative algebra $B$ in $\mathcal V$ has a multiplication $B\otimes B\to B$, a unit $\mathbf1\to B$ and their coherent compatibilities. A left $B$-module in $\mathcal M$ has an action $B\otimes m\to m$ with all coherent associativity and unit data; $\operatorname{LMod}_B(\mathcal M)$ retains the coherent action-preserving maps and their higher simplices. All categories and mapping spaces are taken in sufficiently large universes. Fix $B$ and let $U:\operatorname{LMod}_B(\mathcal M)\to\mathcal M$ forget the action. A morphism of left $B$-modules is an equivalence if and only if its image under $U$ is an equivalence.

Let $K$ be a small simplicial set, let $p:K\to\operatorname{LMod}_B(\mathcal M)$ be a coherent diagram, and suppose there is a colimiting cocone $c:Up\to\Delta_K m$ in $\mathcal M$ such that $v\otimes c$ is colimiting for every $v\in\mathcal V$. Then $p$ admits a colimiting cocone whose underlying cocone is equivalent to $c$. Under these hypotheses an arbitrary cocone $\widetilde c:p\to\Delta_K N$ in $\operatorname{LMod}_B(\mathcal M)$ is colimiting if and only if $U\widetilde c$ is colimiting in $\mathcal M$. The preservation hypothesis concerns only the specified cocone $c$, not every diagram of shape $K$.

source.place: Higher Algebra, Corollaries 4.2.3.2 and 4.2.3.5, printed pp. 527-528; the conservativity is the fixed-algebra consequence of 4.2.3.2, also explicitly recalled after Proposition 4.2.4.9. Online 2017 source read; WANTED: archived Higher Algebra in literature/. No Stacks tag covers coherent infinity-categorical modules.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-coherent-module-section-model] to the given action and $B$, obtaining $q_B:X_B\to S=N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ and the fully faithful module realization $\Gamma_I(q_B)\subseteq\Gamma(q_B)$. Evaluation at each $[n]$ is naturally $U$. The inclusion of $\Gamma(q_B)$ into $\operatorname{Fun}(S,X_B)$ is fully faithful in this particular base: the mapping space from $\mathrm{id}_S$ to itself in $\operatorname{Fun}(S,S)$ is the singleton. Indeed it is the discrete set of natural endomorphisms of the identity of $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$; naturality against the arrows opposite to all vertex inclusions $[0]\to[n]$ forces every component to fix each vertex of $[n]$, hence to be the identity. More explicitly, $\operatorname{Fun}(N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}),N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}))$ is the nerve of the ordinary functor category: an $r$-simplex on either side is exactly a functor $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\times[r]\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$. Every mapping simplex between identity functors is therefore constant. Consequently every mapping simplex between two sections already lies over the identity, so their right-pinched mapping simplicial sets in sections and in the ambient functor category are literally the same. By [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences], a transformation of module sections is an equivalence precisely when all its evaluations are equivalences; each is naturally $U$ of the module map. This proves the equivalence clause independently of any colimits. Functors preserve equivalences by applying them to an inverse and its inverse homotopies.

source.place: Corollary 4.2.2.16 and Remark 4.2.2.19; fixed-algebra conservativity in Corollary 4.2.3.2.

proof.text: Regard $p$ as a diagram $P:K\to\Gamma_I(q_B)$. Under each fiber equivalence its evaluation is naturally $Up$, so the specified cocone $c$ gives a colimiting fiber cocone $c_n$ at every $[n]$. For an edge opposite to $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, the model [lem-coef-coherent-module-section-model] identifies its local transport with $B^{\otimes r}\otimes-$, where $r=n-\alpha(m)\geq0$. For $r>0$ its image of $c_n$ is colimiting by the hypothesis on $v=B^{\otimes r}$; for $r=0$ it is equivalent to $c$ by the coherent unit constraint. Thus the exact diagram-specific transport hypotheses of [lem-coef-local-transport-section-colimits] hold. That node supplies a colimit cocone $C:P\to\Delta_K L$ in all sections, with every evaluation equivalent to $c_n$. No global supply of colimits, and no preservation by the tensor product in its first variable, has been used.

source.place: Proof of Corollary 4.2.3.5, application of Lemma 3.2.2.9 to the module section model.

proof.text:
Use the cocone mapping-space criterion and equivalence of mapping spaces in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. The section $L$ satisfies the module condition. For an arrow $\beta\in I$ opposite to a final interval inclusion $\alpha:[m]\hookrightarrow[n]$, one has $\alpha(m)=n$ and hence $r=0$. Its local transport is therefore the identity under the fiber identifications, by [lem-coef-coherent-module-section-model]. The maps of $P(k)$ over $\beta$ give a pointwise equivalence $P_n\to P_m$, because $P(k)$ is a module section. Naturality of $C$ says that the map $L_n\to L_m$ induced by its edge over $\beta$ intertwines the colimit cocones $C_n$ and $C_m$ with this equivalence. For every $z\in\mathcal M$, precomposition with this map identifies with the composite
$$\operatorname{Map}(L_m,z)\simeq\operatorname{Cocone}(P_m,z)\simeq\operatorname{Cocone}(P_n,z)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(L_n,z).$$
Here the middle equivalence is precomposition with the inverse-equivalent diagram map. It follows directly that $L_n\to L_m$ is invertible: test $z=L_n$ for a left inverse, and then $z=L_m$ for the other inverse equation, retaining the homotopies. The model's arrow criterion therefore makes the edge locally cocartesian. This holds for every $\beta\in I$, so $L\in\Gamma_I(q_B)$.

source.place: Proof of Corollary 4.2.3.5: the pointwise colimit section still belongs to LMod; inert condition of Remark 4.2.2.19.

proof.text: Use the cocone mapping-space criterion and equivalence of mapping spaces in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Since the module sections form a full subcategory and the vertex $L$ is in it, the cocone $C$ is colimiting there: for any module section $N$, both its mapping space out of $L$ and the space of cocones from $P$ to $N$ are the same as in all sections. The equivalence of these spaces for $C$ is its colimit universal property. Under [lem-coef-coherent-module-section-model] this gives a colimiting module cocone $\widehat c$ with vertex $\widehat L$. Its underlying cocone is the evaluation at $[0]$ of $C$, hence equivalent to the specified $c$ by Step 2. This proves the asserted existence with the specified underlying cocone, rather than only existence of an unrelated colimit.

source.place: Proof of Corollary 4.2.3.5(1), restriction from all sections to the full module subcategory.

proof.text: Use the cocone mapping-space criterion and equivalence of mapping spaces in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Let $\widetilde c:p\to\Delta_K N$ be any module cocone. The module colimit $\widehat c$ gives a comparison $a:\widehat L\to N$ together with its coherent equality of cocones $a\widehat c\simeq\widetilde c$. If $U\widetilde c$ is colimiting, $Ua$ compares two colimit cocones on $Up$, so it is an equivalence: their universal mapping-space properties give inverse comparisons and homotopies of both composites to the identities. Step 1 then makes $a$ an equivalence, and composing the universal mapping-space equivalence for $\widehat c$ with this equivalence shows $\widetilde c$ is colimiting. Conversely if $\widetilde c$ is colimiting, the same inverse-comparison argument in modules makes $a$ an equivalence; applying $U$ makes its cocone equivalent to $U\widehat c\simeq c$, which is colimiting. This proves both directions using only the chosen cocone hypothesis.

source.place: Final comparison-map paragraph in the proof of Corollary 4.2.3.5(2).
